exposure: tranexamic acid impregnated in a gelatin sponge
outcome: Amount and nature of discharge collected from the sub-rectus drain
Complications (rectus sheath hematoma, wound infection, thromboembolism)
cohort: 63 pregnant women undergoing elective Cesarean section, on antenatal warfarin anticoagulation from 13 to 36 weeks gestation, then switched to LMWH or UFH, and with an indication for postnatal warfarin anticoagulation
finding: Tranexamic acid-soaked gelatin sponges were safe and effective in reducing postoperative drainage and estimated blood loss in women undergoing Cesarean section who were on warfarin therapy.
